standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the Cartier zero scheme Z of the regular section, its dimension 0, and the exact sequences 0 -> L^tensor n -> L^tensor n+1 -> i_*(L^tensor n+1|_Z) -> 0.

standard_prerequisites.name: Proj of a section ring generated in bounded degree
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies X = Proj(S) for S the section ring and converts generation of the Veronese S^(6) in degree 1 into very-ampleness of L^tensor 6.

core_obligations: Setup and vanishing (proof lines 1524-1556): the zero scheme Z of a regular section s is 0-dimensional Artinian with L|_Z = O_Z; the sequences 0 -> L^tensor n -> L^tensor n+1 -> i_*(L^tensor n+1|_Z) -> 0 give H^1(X, L^tensor n) = 0 for n > 0 by induction, and sections t_{n+1} trivializing L^tensor n+1|_Z exist.

Surjectivity of the two-term multiplication map (proof lines 1559-1580): mu_n from H^0(L) x H^0(L^tensor n) plus H^0(L^tensor 2) x H^0(L^tensor n-1) onto H^0(L^tensor n+1) is surjective for n >= 3, since sections from the left of the divisor sequence lie in the image and mu_n(H^0(L^tensor 2) tensor t_{n-1}) covers the part supported on Z.

Conclusion via the Veronese (proof lines 1583-1600): S = direct sum H^0(X, L^tensor n) is generated in degrees 0, 1, 2, 3; X = Proj(S) by morphisms-lemma-proper-ample-is-proj; hence the sixth Veronese S^(6) is generated in degree 1, which means L^tensor 6 is very ample.
proof_roadmap: Introduce the Cartier zero scheme Z of the regular section and record the tensor-power exact sequences.
Get H^1(X, L^tensor n) = 0 and trivializations t_n on Z by induction.
Prove the two-term multiplication map is surjective for n >= 3, splitting sections along Z.
Conclude generation of S in degrees <= 3 and read very-ampleness of L^tensor 6 off the Veronese.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves a concrete very-ampleness criterion with the exponent 6 (statement lines 1505-1516). The proof (lines 1518-1591) works: the Cartier zero scheme gives induction sequences killing H^1 of all tensor powers and producing trivializing sections on Z, the two-term multiplication map is shown surjective for n >= 3 by splitting sections along Z, and the conclusion runs through generation of the section ring in degrees 0-3 and the Veronese S^(6) generated in degree 1. H2: standard homological algebra with one genuine bookkeeping step (the two-term multiplication map), executed fully in the span.
